title: Sequentializable eviction protocol with batch-awareness for KV cache correctness
creator: Avery Martinez
description: Problem statement: Continuous batching reduces per-token latency and cost but complicates KV cache correctness when eviction (LRU/TTL/prefix-aware) happens concurrently with in-flight batch processing. We observed two classes of correctness bugs in canaries: (1) stale KV references returned to the runtime after eviction+reclamation leading to incorrect generation state, and (2) lost prefix-affinity where a newly scheduled batch expects pinned prefix entries that were concurrently evicted due to TTL heuristics. Goal: design and implement a sequentializable eviction protocol that is batch-aware and GPU-memory friendly. The protocol must provide clear operational invariants (no use-after-free of KV entries, deterministic prefix pin semantics for batches started under specific prefixes, bounded latency for eviction under pressure) while minimizing additional allocation overhead on GPU memory and avoiding global JVM/host locks that hurt throughput.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Formal invariants documented: (a) KV entry never referenced after reclamation; (b) batch start pins its prefix snapshot until batch complete or explicit release; (b) TTL expiry cannot race to free entries referenced by an in-flight batch.
2) Implementation of fencing tokens for batch lifecycle so evictors only reclaim entries with fencing <= retired epoch.
3) Integration tests: deterministic harness that repros prior canary failures cannot fail after change (1000 seed fuzz, 10k synthetic batches).

4) Performance: end-to-end p50 generation latency degradation <= 5% under normal load vs baseline; under high memory pressure, eviction throughput improves reclamation latency by >= 20% without correctness regressions.
5) Rollout plan and feature flag implemented; canary on dedicated infra with sampling of live traffic for 48h before full release.
design_notes: High-level design: Introduce a lightweight epoch-based fencing token associated with each batch and with each pinned prefix reference. When a batch is scheduled, it obtains a monotonic batch_epoch and records batch_epoch on any KV entries it reads/uses. Eviction proceeds only if the candidate entry's last_seen_epoch < global_retention_epoch (epoch advanced only after all batches that could reference it have completed). For TTL-driven eviction, we retain a soft-ttl state and convert to hard-ttl only when fencing indicates no active batch could reference the entry. For prefix-aware eviction, keep a small per-prefix active_count that increments on batch start and decrements on completion; eviction of prefix-scoped slabs is gated on active_count==0 OR the fencing epoch check. GPU memory optimization: avoid per-entry locks by storing epochs and refcounts in compact 32-bit structures; reclamation uses hazard-pointer-style atomic CAS with a tombstone step to let in-flight batches detect and finish gracefully. We prefer epoch stamping over heavyweight GC or per-batch pin queues to keep hot-path allocations minimal.
implementation_plan: 1) Add batch_epoch allocator in runtime scheduler and API hook at batch start/finish (scheduler change). 2) Extend KV entry header with fields: last_seen_epoch, ttl_soft_expiry, tombstone_flag (packed into 64-bit). 3) Update eviction worker: consult last_seen_epoch + per-prefix active_count before reclaiming; tombstone->reclaim flow is two-step to let racing readers observe tombstone and stop using entry. 4) Add per-prefix active_count increment/decrement on batch lifecycle. 5) Add feature flag 'evict.batch-aware.v1' and test hooks. 6) Add low-level GPU-side atomic ops for marking tombstone and reclamation (CUDA kernels & CPU fallback). 7) Unit tests, integration harness, and canary rollout (see test_plan/rollout_plan).
test_plan: - Unit tests for batch_epoch allocation and wraparound semantics. - Property-based tests: fuzz sequences of batch starts/completions, TTL expiries, LRU promotions, and ensure invariants hold. - Deterministic replay harness: record schedule traces from production-like load (including continuous batching) and replay under stress to confirm no use-after-free. - GPU regression tests that ensure per-entry header fits in existing slab metadata and that reclamation path works on small and large slabs. - Performance benchmark comparisons: baseline vs feature flag under low and high memory pressure. - Safety canary: enable feature on 2 dedicated hosts serving 5% of traffic for 48 hours with strict logging of any tombstone races.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'evict.batch-aware.v1'. Stages: (A) Internal QA on staging cluster (2 days); (B) Canary on dedicated infra (2 hosts, 5% traffic, 48h); (C) Expanded canary (20% traffic, 72h) with automated rollback if any correctness assertion triggers; (D) Full release to runtime-1.22 if canary metrics stable. Rollout will include added telemetry: tombstone_count, reclaimed_with_epoch, prefix_eviction_blocked_count, and per-host reclamation_latency histograms.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket opened. Initial design sketch reviewed with runtime and kernels teams. Blocking question: epoch allocator wrap semantics under long-running hosts (discussed to use 64-bit monotonic counter with periodic compaction).
2026-03-11: Prototype of batch_epoch allocator completed by Liam Chen (branch: feat/epoch-allocator). Basic unit tests added. Requested review from Priya Rao (runtime).
2026-03-12: Design review notes: Priya suggested tombstone two-step flow to avoid CAS contention; Diego (kernels) requested compact header layout for GPU efficiency. Updated design_notes accordingly.
2026-03-13: Implemented per-prefix active_count and added test hooks in scheduler. Observed trivial p95 latency bump in microbenchmarks (~3%). Preparing integration fuzz harness configs.
2026-03-14: First-run deterministic replay completed against a recorded trace of 120k batches; no use-after-free observed. Creating PR and adding reviewers: @priya-rao, @diego-kernels, @maria-ops.
